profile._note: Curated page text, rendered by the pages at runtime. Strings allow [label](url), **bold** and {{tokens}} (e.g. {{short}}, {{poss}}). Every fact typed here also goes in data/claims_static.json with its source.
profile.lede: A running check of what Garcia promised voters in CA-42, what he has done in office, and what he says on the issues people are fighting about. Every entry links to its source.

facts.label: 2026 general
facts.value: Re-elected 62.0% to 38.0% over Brian Burley (R), unofficial, all precincts reporting

facts.label: Background
facts.value: Former mayor of Long Beach; first LGBTQ+ immigrant to serve in Congress

factSources: 2026 general (unofficial, all 402 precincts reporting, read Nov 25, 2026): Garcia 175,590 (62.0%), Burley 107,781 (38.0%). [CA Secretary of State](https://api.sos.ca.gov/returns/us-rep/district/42)

Ranking Member: elected by House Democrats 150-63 on Jun 24, 2025. [His office](https://robertgarcia.house.gov/media/press-releases/congressman-robert-garcia-statement-election-ranking-member-house-oversight)

Background: [his 2024 campaign site, archived Oct 31, 2024](https://web.archive.org/web/20241031202426/https://robertgarcia.com/about/) (mayor); [his office](https://robertgarcia.house.gov/media/press-releases/historic-first-congressman-robert-garcia-finally-sworn-us-house) (first LGBTQ+ immigrant to serve in Congress).

committees.name: Oversight and Government Reform Committee
committees.blurb: The House's main investigative committee, with authority to examine any matter within the jurisdiction of the other committees. As Ranking Member he is the top Democrat on it.

committees.name: Transportation and Infrastructure Committee
committees.blurb: Oversees aviation, highways and transit, ports and waterways, and the Coast Guard, all central to Long Beach.

events.intro: Public events where Garcia appears in Long Beach and beyond, from his press releases. His office does not list town halls on its site.
events.ask: His website and press releases list no upcoming town halls. Call the Long Beach district office at (562) 512-8489 to ask when the next one will be, or see every way to reach him on the [Overview](./#channels).

map.heading: CA-42 is moving to Long Beach and coastal Orange County
map.intro: Prop 50 redrew the lines for the 2026 election, and Garcia was re-elected under the new map. The new map takes effect Jan 3, 2027; until then he represents the 2023 lines, which include Long Beach, Downey and Huntington Park.
map.note: Shaded areas are the parts of each city inside the district; the dark line is the district boundary. Boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb (119th and 120th Congressional Districts). Population figures: 2020 Census, from the [California Senate Office of Demographics](https://sdmg.senate.ca.gov/committeehome/2025-congressional-districts/congressional-district-42-2025). Current lines: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California%27s_42nd_congressional_district). [Official boundary map](https://sdmg.senate.ca.gov/sites/sdmg.senate.ca.gov/files/2026-02/cd42_2025.png).
map._note: modes: build_map.py writes 'new' (cd120) and 'old' (cd119). population: {mode, total, parts: [[kind, label, residents, note]], source}.
map.leavingNote: Leaving the district under Prop 50 (cities of 10,000 or more): Downey, Lakewood, Bellflower, Florence-Graham, Huntington Park, Bell Gardens, Bell, Maywood, Cudahy, Walnut Park and Commerce. Long Beach shrinks to part of the city.

placeStats._note: Residents of each city inside the 2027 district and the share of the city's population, from the California Senate Office of Demographics (2020 Census). 'old' is w (whole) or p (part) when the city was in the 2023-26 district, empty when new.
